title: adaptive-latency-smoothing-and-payload-guardrails-for-gateway
author: Maya Chen
description: Introduce adaptive latency smoothing and conservative payload guardrails at the API gateway to stabilize streaming sessions and preserve OpenAI-compat behavior. This PR tunes the streaming proxy buffer growth to be KV-cache-aware, prioritizes small tool/function-call payloads in routing decisions, enforces early-reject guardrails for oversized multipart/attachment metadata to avoid noisy upstream resource usage, and adds a content-negotiation handshake for structured output via the compat layer. Motivation: we've observed transient streaming stalls and client timeouts when large metadata-prefixed requests depleted proxy headroom or caused rebuffer thrash; this change reduces those incidents without changing model runtime code. Change summary: 1) adaptive-proxy-buffer: new algorithm that grows buffer windows based on per-route observed token churn and KV-cache hit-rate; 2) route-prioritizer: route scoring tweaks to prefer small toolcall routes when queue depth > 8; 3) payload-guardrails: 413 early-reject for metadata > 256KB and structured-output header validation returns 400 with guidance; 4) compat-handshake: small client/server negotiate to fall back to non-streaming or chunked-mode when streaming framing isn't supported. Includes tests for route scoring and simulated high-concurrency streaming sessions. See linear ENG-4982 for perf graphs and incident correlation.

notes_for_oncall: If customers report new 413s, check gateway.payload_guard.reject_count and route-specific max_buffer_bytes. The circuit-breaker will auto-relax under healthy memory pressure but can be tuned per-customer via route config.
